In the toy models, they show that $c_{dec}$ can be used to identify the correct $L_0$ that avoids feature mixing. In the LLM experiments, they demonstrate that the minimum of the $c_{dec}$ curve often aligns with the $L_0$ value that yields the best performance on sparse probing tasks, suggesting that their metric can be a useful tool for selecting the appropriate sparsity level in real-world scenarios. The paper's main contribution lies in highlighting the importance of selecting the correct $L_0$ for SAEs, demonstrating the limitations of relying solely on sparsity-reconstruction tradeoffs, and proposing a practical metric to guide the selection of $L_0$. The authors also provide a theoretical justification for their metric in Appendix A.6, further strengthening their claims. My confidence in this weakness is high, as the paper does not provide the necessary details for reproducibility.
